performed_via_github_app.description:
Publish incredibly high performance websites and applications right from GitHub. The Netlify platform connects your repositories to an all-in-one workflow for global CDN deployment, continuous integration, and automatic (and free) HTTPS. Each time you commit changes, Netlify builds your site, prerenders markup, and optimizes assets on dedicated build infrastructure. Easily create an entirely automated workflows for your web applications

## Features

### Push your site live, directly from GitHub
Deploy your site to an ultra-redundant global CDN that’s purpose built for serving pages and assets quickly and consistently.

### Automate deployment
Netlify’s built-in Continuous Deployment automatically runs your build commands and deploys the result whenever you push to your Git repository.

### Add a custom domain
Purchase domains and manage DNS zones and records right inside of Netlify.

### HTTPS is automatic
Your site will automatically be secured with a free TLS certificate from Let’s Encrypt.

### Deploy Previews
Netlify’s Deploy Previews streamlined your workflow by giving you a unique, permanent URL to check what your changes will be like in production whenever you submit a pull request.

### And a lot more!
Netlify includes solutions for forms, identity, and even custom functions powered by AWS Lambda. And all this functionality can be configured directly in your repo.

> (2) Replace the console.error substring spy with a direct flushSync spy.

I disagree with this one since the original issue is about the error appearing during a specific React phase, and this tests that more directly. Checking if `flushSync` was called doesn't test the timing of the call. The error messages haven't changed in a long time so that's not a valid concern imo

Addressed others

## Code Review (GPT-5.5 + Opus 4.7)
Approve ✅ The patch removes the lifecycle `flushSync` dependency while preserving synchronous submit blocking through the form registry, and the targeted regression coverage/typecheck look solid.

### 1. Bugs / Issues (None)

No concrete blocking, non-blocking, or informational issues found.

### Root Cause & Patch Assessment

The fix addresses the real submit-time requirement: validation no longer needs React state to flush synchronously because `validate()` now updates the form registry’s `validityData` before submit checks read it. The registered-control id handoff also keeps non-native field controls, same-name fields, and control replacement scoped to the correct registry entry.

### Repo Conventions / Cleanliness Assessment

The changed code follows the local hook conventions: `useStableCallback` remains on effect/event-facing callbacks, `useIsoLayoutEffect` usage is unchanged where needed, and the tests stick to Vitest/testing-library matcher style.

### Test Coverage Assessment

Validated locally:

- `pnpm test:jsdom Form --no-watch`
- `pnpm test:jsdom OTPField --no-watch`
- `pnpm typescript`

The new OTP auto-submit regression tests were also applied to the PR merge-base implementation and failed there, confirming they catch the removed `flushSync` lifecycle warning path.
